scope: Third synthetic pure-text development round; manual clause-level semantic review of baseline versus source-minimal; proposal-only and not production adoption.

automated_triage.warning: All structured fields passed, but this did not score learner_prompt semantics.

manual_review_policy.method: Read every source, task and final Draft clause by clause. Ordinary recall, restatement and self-check activities were allowed; source-external facts, event types, real-world operations and delivery mechanisms were not.

manual_findings.finding: Baseline invented a submission mechanism; source-minimal stayed with listing and restatement.
Both preserved sequence without converting it to causality.
Baseline requested an unstated survey object and real-world transect procedure during the study window; source-minimal limited the task to supplied fields.
Baseline invented a study-log delivery arrangement.
Baseline asked what action waiting requires although the source establishes no required action.
Baseline replaced the supplied routing note with a presumed separately accessible register.
Baseline changed shift note to handoff log; source-minimal instead invented submission.
Source-minimal turned a scheduled record into real filter removal, housing inspection, new-filter installation and seal confirmation.
Both remained a card-reading or recall exercise and did not operate the valve.
Baseline strengthened visit into appointment; source-minimal retained the source event.

paired_cluster_audit.baseline_major_pattern: Learner prompt asks for a real-world action or procedural answer that the source cannot supply.

limitations: Synthetic development cases and internal manual review do not constitute an independent holdout.
The source-minimal arm used 30.7 percent more reported tokens than baseline and still produced one major regression.
No domain admission, commit, read-back or UI delivery was tested.
